findings.desc: CHK-002 adversarial verificationIntent says a run must HARD_FAIL when lifecycle evidence linkage drops below 1, but the recorded verificationEvidence points to memory-benchmark-smoke and that smoke test only asserts the happy-path value equals 1.0; it never exercises a <1 linkage override or checks the resulting HARD_FAIL, so this must-intent branch is not mechanically covered.
findings.resolvedReason: Fixed by commit 96406b20: memory benchmark smoke now constructs lifecycleGateEvidenceLinkageRate below 1 and asserts evidenceLinkageRateLifecycleGate < 1, verdict HARD_FAIL, thresholdPassed false, and unchanged memoryScore. Revalidated with npm --prefix packages/main run test:memory-benchmark-smoke, npm --prefix packages/main run build, and koala validate covering 9/9 verification intents.

findings.desc: memory_benchmark_compare accepts arbitrary candidateCounts, but resolveMemoryBenchmarkTierConfig maps any unmapped count >=10000 to tier T3 with threshold=null. Repro: `node bin/koala.js memory_benchmark_compare --candidateCounts=50000 --format=json` returns `{ tier: "T3", candidateCount: 50000 }`, which contradicts the documented fixed tier contract (10k/100k/1M) and makes the report semantically misleading. Reject unsupported counts or introduce an explicit custom tier/threshold contract, and add smoke coverage for this edge case.
findings.resolvedReason: Fixed by commit 192f5ef2: unsupported fixed-tier candidate counts now throw an explicit error instead of being labeled T3; smoke covers run and compare unsupported-count paths. Revalidated with npm --prefix packages/main run test:memory-benchmark-smoke, npm --prefix packages/main run build, node bin/koala.js memory_benchmark_compare --candidateCounts=50000 --format=json (clean rejection), and 10k/100k/1M compare output preserving PASS metrics.
